title: Incident closure: guardrails & hardenings workshop
summary: Redwood + Greenfield met to close out the recent inference service degradation. Reviewed timeline, possible root causes (KV cache eviction patterns + bursty prefix traffic), agreed temporary mitigations (throttle + canary fallback), and drafted a set of guardrails: alert thresholds, runbook steps, and an oncall handoff. MVP deliverables: trimmed logs + sample traces, runbook draft, and a scheduled benchmark for dedicated capacity. Next checkpoint: 2026-09-03 for runbook review and test plan signoff.
action_items: Maya Patel — Share trimmed logs and kafka-ish trace excerpt for 2026-08-18 window (due 2026-09-01)
Diego Ruiz — Provide suggested alert thresholds and sample Grafana dashboard JSON (due 2026-09-02)
Ravi Kumar — Confirm oncall rotation changes and contact info for pager handoff (due 2026-09-01)
Marta Silva — Confirm compliance gating for Private deployment (KMS/HSM questions) and list required audit logs (due 2026-09-04)
Lina Gomez — Schedule 60-min benchmark test with Redwood Dedicated team and share calendar invite (due 2026-09-03)
next_steps: Run focused benchmark on dedicated pool with sample workload (Diego + Lina)
Redwood to send runbook draft and fallback playbook (Maya)
Greenfield to evaluate alert thresholds and adjust SRE runbook (Ravi)
Legal/security sync if Private deployment is pursued (Marta + Redwood security)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Alice (Greenfield), Ravi (Greenfield SRE), Marta (Greenfield Sec)

Auto-Summary: Short call to close incident and agree on guardrails/hardenings - medium transcription quality, some words garbled.

[00:00:05] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know this is a tight window, so we'll run through timeline and focus on concrete next steps. Diego, can you start with the brief RCA hypothesis?

[00:00:22] Diego (Redwood SE): Sure, uh, hi. So quick summary — what we saw was a compounding effect. There was a burst of prefix-heavy traffic which increased KV cache misses, the eviction policy kicked in, and that caused more token re-computation; latencies spiked and some requests crossed the SLA. We're still correlating with the autoscaler events but the pattern points to repeated cold KV misses rather than a single host failure.

[00:00:45] Ravi (Greenfield SRE): Sorry to interrupt — when you say KV cache evictions, do you mean our cache on the model side or the app-side cache? We have a Redis in front and then the model KV.

[00:00:55] Diego (Redwood SE): Good q, it's the model-side KV cache — the attention KV that the runtime keeps. There might also be amplification from our Redis TTLs but primary latency came from re-computing context.

[00:01:10] Alice (Greenfield): Just to add context, we had a campaign launch the morning of the 18th that sent large numbers of short prompts with similar prefixes. Our traffic team changed the batching behavior temporarily which probably made it worse.

[00:01:28] Maya (Redwood): Okay that matches what we saw. For mitigations we proposed three parallel things: immediate throttle and canary fallback to smaller model variant, a temporary cache warm strategy, and an oncall escalation flow with documented thresholds.

[00:01:43] Marta (Greenfield): From security side: if we do private deployment or dedicated pools, we need to know what audit logs Redwood can emit, and how KMS integration looks. SOC2 stuff — we need to capture key material rotation events.

[00:02:02] Diego (Redwood SE): Sure, we can produce audit log types: request metadata, model version, decision to fallback, evictions, and key usage stamps. For KMS we support common providers and HSM integrations on Private offerings, but we'll share the security doc; there might be slight mis-terms in the auto transcript.

[00:02:25] Ravi (Greenfield SRE): Walk me through the short term playbook — like during a spike, what do we flip?

[00:02:30] Maya (Redwood): Step 1, trigger a canary fallback route that directs a small percentage to a smaller model variant with a harder timeout, step 2, limit per-client rate at the edge for prefix-heavy signatures, step 3, warm prefix cache for the most frequent prefixes if we can precompute.

[00:02:49] Diego (Redwood SE): Also, for immediate observability we recommended instrumenting a per-prefix miss-rate metric and an eviction-rate metric. If eviction-rate > 0.4 and tail-latency > 2x baseline then auto-fallback. That's just a starting heuristic.

[00:03:05] Alice (Greenfield): Is that something Redwood can push as a managed alert or we need to add it to our Grafana?

[00:03:09] Diego (Redwood SE): We can push dashboard JSON and suggested alert rules, but Greenfield will need to map them into your monitoring stack (we provided Grafana/Prometheus examples previously).

[00:03:22] Lina (Redwood CSM): I'll coordinate the dashboard handoff and calendar the benchmark.

[00:03:29] Marta (Greenfield): On compliance — for Private envs, will we see full request bodies in logs? We can't have PHI leaving systems.

[00:03:36] Maya (Redwood): Good point. We can redact request content from logs and only emit metadata. For Private we support customer-managed VPCs and KMS so keys never leave your boundary. We'll attach the security PDF.

[00:03:50] Ravi (Greenfield): In terms of runbook language, can you write a very concrete step-by-step for the oncall? Last time the notes were high-level and folks were unsure.

[00:03:58] Diego (Redwood SE): Absolutely — we'll produce a runbook with exact command lines, thresholds, and fallback toggles (including which route to flip in the load balancer). We'll avoid ambiguous phrasing.

[00:04:10] Alice (Greenfield): Can you also include the rollback path? If the fallback increases error types downstream we need a quick way to revert.

[00:04:15] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, rollback instructions, plus a quick smoke test to validate client-visible regression.

[00:04:24] Maya (Redwood): For ownership, Lina will schedule the benchmark; Diego will author the runbook and dashboard; Maya will send logs and a short post-incident note for legal and execs. Marta you'll validate compliance gating. Ravi you'll confirm oncall contact updates.

[00:04:36] Marta (Greenfield): Quick Q — if we move to Dedicated capacity, will that change the evictions behavior you observed?

[00:04:42] Diego (Redwood SE): It could. Dedicated gives predictable capacity and lets you pin working set sizes to a GPU pool so eviction churn is reduced. But we also recommended model-quantization or slightly higher memory configs to further reduce evictions. We'll propose a bench plan that shows tradeoffs.

[00:04:59] Alice (Greenfield): Any cost ballpark for that dedicated test? We want to get budget approval.

[00:05:04] Maya (Redwood): The bench for a day is minimal; we'll include a cost estimate in the invite. If you decide to go full Dedicated it becomes a reserved contract. Lina will include pricing bands.

[00:05:18] Ravi (Greenfield): About the alerts — we saw noisy alerts last time. Can we have a staging-to-prod threshold so we don't get paged for non-impacting variance?

[00:05:25] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, absolute thresholds plus sustained-duration conditions (e.g. > 5 minutes) and correlation with error-rate to avoid noise.

[00:05:36] Alice (Greenfield): A small nit — the auto transcript shows "kay vee" as K-V, that's fine but in our docs it's spelled KV.

[00:05:42] Diego (Redwood SE): Yep, common OCR-ish thing.

[00:05:45] Maya (Redwood): Moving to timelines — we agreed the runbook draft by 2026-09-02, benchmark scheduled 2026-09-03, and follow-up checkpoint 2026-09-03 15:00 UTC. Any blocking items?

[00:05:58] Ravi (Greenfield): We need the trimmed logs to correlate with our app telemetry. If you can send them with the exact timestamps that will help.

[00:06:04] Maya (Redwood): We'll send trimmed logs with time windows and a short readme.

[00:06:10] Marta (Greenfield): Also, include the exact fields present in audit logs and a sample sanitized entry.

[00:06:15] Diego (Redwood SE): Will do.

[00:06:20] Lina (Redwood CSM): I'll send the calendar invite now and mark action owners.

[00:06:26] Alice (Greenfield): Cool. One last item — are there any dependencies on our infra changes from the campaign team? They changed the batching previously.

[00:06:33] Maya (Redwood): If traffic characteristics change, the mitigation thresholds must be adapted. We'll include guidance on how to tune alerts per traffic profile.

[00:06:42] Ravi (Greenfield): Ok sounds good.

[00:06:45] Maya (Redwood): Alright, recap: Diego runbook+dashboard (due 09-02), Maya trimmed logs+PI summary (09-01), Lina benchmark invite+pricing (09-03), Marta compliance gating checklist (09-04), Ravi confirm oncall contacts (09-01). Follow-up 09-03 15:00 UTC. Anything else?

[00:06:59] Marta (Greenfield): No, thanks everyone.

[00:07:02] Alice (Greenfield): Thanks.

[00:07:04] Maya (Redwood): Thanks all — we'll follow up in email. End call.

Notes: Transcript has periodic timestamps from beginning; the call continued with low-volume side chat as people dropped but major decisions captured above. Some words in transcription may be slightly off (KMS vs KMS provider names, "kay vee" vs KV). Links shared: Security PDF (redwood.ai/security.pdf) and runbook template (link in follow-up).
